brief: Treasuries pause on Tuesday but rate vol and payer skew stay rich, signaling the market remains wary of another leg higher in yields. Bear steepening stays the dominant theme. Softer payrolls and more patient Fed rhetoric cut October hike odds below 25%, letting the front end outperform, but a less urgent Fed doesn't imply a lower terminal rate or ease fiscal deficit and heavy Treasury supply concerns, so the long end hasn't benefited. ISM Services Prices Paid jumped to 74, the highest since July 2022, and energy cost uncertainty plus AI capex demand reinforce the case for yields grinding higher. The MOVE Index is near its highest this year and TLT's one month implied vol sits at the 98th to 100th percentile, versus subdued equity vol. Citi finds long expiry payer skew and Treasury put skew rich, meaning investors pay an unusually high premium for protection against further yield rises. Rising yields can self reinforce through mortgage duration hedging that adds selling pressure. The market is technically oversold with no clear reversal catalyst. Deutsche Bank sees CTAs heavily short bonds, while JPMorgan's clients are net long. This week's 10 and 30 year auctions matter more than usual: clean absorption points to stabilization, a weak reception would confirm yields haven't hit cycle highs.
